subject: Creativity
title: Show, Don't Tell: Writing's Golden Rule
description: A quick win: understand Show, Don't Tell: Writing's Golden Rule.

hook.text: 'She was sad' is telling. 'She stared at the untouched cake, pressing her thumb into the frosting' is showing.

buildup.text: Chekhov wrote: 'Don't tell me the moon is shining; show me the glint of light on broken glass.

discovery.text: Showing activates the reader's imagination. Telling bypasses it.

twist.text: But great writers break this rule constantly. 'It was the best of times, it was the worst of times' — pure telling.

climax.text: The real rule: show emotions, tell logistics. Nobody needs to 'experience' a character driving to the airport.

punchline.text: Show when it matters. Tell when it doesn't. That's the actual rule.

quiz.question: Which famous author said 'show me the glint of light on broken glass'?

details.summary: Show don't tell means conveying information through action, dialogue, and sensory detail rather than direct statement. Instead of writing she was angry, show her slamming a door and speaking through clenched teeth. It makes writing vivid and immersive.
details.whyItMatters: Showing engages the reader's imagination and creates emotional involvement. Telling keeps readers at a distance. This principle separates amateur writing from professional craft.
takeaways: Actions and sensory details are more powerful than statements
Showing invites readers to draw their own conclusions
Strategic telling is still necessary for pacing and transitions

faq.question: Should you never tell in writing?
faq.answer: No. Pure showing would make every story unbearably long. Telling is appropriate for transitions, minor details, and pacing. The skill is knowing what deserves to be shown through scene and what can be efficiently told through summary.

faq.question: How do you practice showing instead of telling?
faq.answer: Take a simple emotional statement like he was nervous and rewrite it using only physical actions and sensory details. Describe what nervous looks like from the outside. Repeat this exercise with different emotions until it becomes instinctive.
